title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Commanders D/ST allows 37 points in Week 2 loss
items.desc: The Commanders D/ST allowed 37 points, 279 passing yards, and 66 rushing yards in the loss to the Cowboys.
items.impact: The Commanders' defense tallied two sacks, but forced no turnovers in the loss to Dallas. They did a great job limiting the Cowboys rushing attack to 3.1 yards per carry. The Commanders' defense will need to be solid if they hope to win against Seattle in Week 3.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Drew Stevens connects on two field goals in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Drew Stevens made 2-of-3 field goals and 2-of-2 extra point attempts in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys.
items.impact: Stevens connected on field goals from 27 yards and 47 yards out, but missed a 51-yarder late in the third quarter. Stevens has now missed three kicks in the first two weeks of the season. Fantasy managers may want to find another option heading into a Week 3 matchup with Seattle.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Antonio Williams hauls in three passes in Week 2
items.desc: Antonio Williams caught all three of his targets for 24 yards in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys.
items.impact: Williams saw his production dip from a strong Week 1 performance. The rookie wide receiver figures to lose some fantasy value with Jayden Daniels sidelined with an elbow injury. Williams and the Commanders will take on the Seahawks in Week 3.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Stefon Diggs hauls in two touchdowns in Week 2
items.desc: Stefon Diggs caught 5-of-6 targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys.
items.impact: Diggs caught touchdowns from both Jayden Daniels and Marcus Maroita to account for both of the team's touchdowns. Diggs has turned in two strong games in his first season in Washington. Diggs and the Commanders will take on the Seahawks in Week 3.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Terry McLaurin quiet in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Terry McLaurin caught 2-of-9 targets for 50 yards in the Commanders loss to Dallas.
items.impact: McLaurin saw a major increase in targets from Week 1, but his production continued to be limited. With Jayden Daniels out, McLaurin could see an increase in targets considering his rapport with Marcus Maroita. McLaurin and the Commanders will take on the Seahawks in Week 3.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Rachaad White hauls in six passes in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Rachaad White rushed for 43 yards on seven carries in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys. He caught 6-of-6 targets for 40 yards.
items.impact: White saw six targets to Jacory Croskey-Merritt's one target, but both contributed the same amount of yards on the ground. With Jayden Daniels (elbow) out for the foreseeable future, the running game should get more of a focus heading into a Week 3 matchup with Seattle.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Justin Jefferson leads pass-catchers in Week 2 win over Bears
items.desc: Justin Jefferson hauled in three of his six targets for a team-high 55 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Jefferson has made the most of generous involvement in an inconsistent Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, finishing with over 50 receiving yards in each of the first two games. The superstar wideout continues to fall victim to underwhelming quarterback play, with a Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers up next.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt sees 12 carries in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 43 yards on 12 carries and caught his lone target for five yards in the loss to Dallas Sunday.
items.impact: Croskey-Merritt was out targeted by Rachaad White 6-to-1, but each tallied 43 yards on the ground. The Commanders' offense took a massive blow losing Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow, so the running game will likely be relied upon more heading into Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Aaron Jones Sr. leads ground attack in Week 2 win over Bears
items.desc: Aaron Jones Sr. carried the ball 23 times for 105 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Jones Sr. took advantage of his role as the primary ball-carrier as part of an inconsistent Minnesota offense, rushing for 40 or more yards in each of the first two games. The veteran running back will look for more success in a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Marcus Mariota solid after Jayden Daniels exits with an injury
items.desc: Marcus Mariota completed 11-of-16 pass attempts for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders 37-20 loss to the Cowboys. He added three rushing yards on one carry.
items.impact: Mariota came into the game after Jayden Daniels suffered an elbow injury to close out the first half. With Daniels dealing with a dislocated elbow, Mariota will quarterback the team for the foreseeable future, starting with a matchup with Seattle in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jordan Addison sees five targets in Week 2 win
items.desc: Jordan Addison hauled in two of his five targets for 21 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Addison has struggled to make an impact as part of an underwhelming Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, finishing with two receptions or less in each of the first two games. The wideout remains a high-risk pass-catching option in all formats ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: T.J. Hockenson catches three passes in Week 2 win
items.desc: T.J. Hockenson caught three of his four targets for 29 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Hockenson has made the most of modest involvement in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, recording three of more receptions in each of the first two games. The tight end remains one of the more risky pass-catching options for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Ravens D/ST struggles in Week 2 loss
items.desc: The Ravens D/ST allowed 24 pints, 252 yards passing, and 65 rushing yards in the loss to the Saints.
items.impact: The Ravens' defense tallied three sacks but failed to force a turnover in the loss. The Ravens will need to get some of the issues with the pass defense together before taking on Dak Prescott and the Cowboys in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Demond Claiborne catches lone target in Week 2
items.desc: Demond Claiborne caught his only target for two yards in the Vikings' 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
items.impact: Claiborne struggled to make an impact in his debut, finishing second to last on the team in touches in the win. The running back remains more of a risky handcuff option for No. 1 running back Aaron Jones Sr., with a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers up next.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Alec Pierce carted to locker room Sunday night
items.desc: Alec Pierce suffered a non-contact injury while running a route in the first quarter against the Chiefs. He appeared to be favoring his surgically repaired ankle and was taken to the medical tent and then carted to the locker room.
items.impact: Not a good look for Pierce, who has continued to work his way back from an ankle injury all offseason and up until now. Given how he looked and the way he was unable to put weight on it, it's unlikely he will return to the game, but time will tell. Fantasy managers will need to monitor the situation closely.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: DeeJay Dallas sees three touches in Week 2
items.desc: DeeJay Dallas rushed twice for eight yards while also catching his only target for 12 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
items.impact: Dallas remains more of an afterthought in the Minnesota offense early on, recording three touches or less in each of the first two games. The running back can be left off rosters with Aaron Jones Sr. commanding the majority of the backfield work, with a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers up next.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Mark Andrews hauls in six passes in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Mark Andrews caught 6-of-7 targets for 49 yards in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints.
items.impact: Andrews ranked second on the team in targets, receptions, and yardage in the loss Sunday. With Zay Flowers (hamstring) out, Andrews should continue to see an increase in targets behind Rashod Bateman. Andrews and the Ravens will take on the Cowboys in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Josh Oliver catches only target in Week 2
items.desc: Josh Oliver caught his only target for 24 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
items.impact: Oliver has seen minimal involvement in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, finishing with two receptions or less in each of the first two games. The tight end remains best left off rosters in all formats, with a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers up next.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Rashod Bateman scores in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Rashod Bateman caught 7-of-9 targets for 88 yards and a touchdown in the 24-17 loss to the Saints.
items.impact: Bateman found the end zone on a 22-yard touchdown to close out the second half. Bateman was the target of the interception late in the game that allowed the Saints to close out the game. If Zay Flowers (hamstring) is unavailable to play in Week 3, Bateman would serve as the primary wide receiver against Dallas.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Justice Hill quiet in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Justice Hill rushed for six yards on two carries in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints.
items.impact: Hill was uninvolved in the passing game and saw his touches drop from Week 1. Fantasy managers should expect Hill to continue to see limited usage as long as Derrick Henry is healthy.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Derrick Henry finds the end zone in Week 2
items.desc: Derrick Henry rushed for 68 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints. He caught all three of his targets for 19 yards.
items.impact: Henry found the end zone on a one-yard rush in the first quarter. The veteran was held in check after that, unable to find any big gains on the ground. Henry and the Ravens will head to Dallas for a Week 3 matchup with the Cowboys.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Myles Price sees one target in Week 2
items.desc: Myles Price failed to catch his only target in the Vikings' 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
items.impact: Price remains minimally involved in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, recording one target or less in each of the first two games. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Lamar Jackson held in check in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Lamar Jackson completed 21-of-31 passes for 235 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints. He added 34 rushing yards on four carries.
items.impact: Jackson and the Ravens' offense appeared to feel the loss of Zay Flowers (hamstring) who was unavailable for this game. Jackson was intercepted on the final play of the game as the Ravens attempted a late comeback. The Ravens will travel to Dallas to take on the Cowboys in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Carson Wentz quiet in Week 2 win over Bears
items.desc: Carson Wentz completed 11-of-20 pass attempts for 143 yards while also rushing three times for six yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Wentz has struggled to make an impact behind center to begin the season, finishing with less than 145 passing yards in each of the first two games. The quarterback could be relegated to the bench if No. 1 signal-caller Kyler Murray (concussion) is able to suit up for a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Saints D/ST allows 17 points in Week 2 win
items.desc: The Saints D/ST allowed 17 points, 235 passing yards, and 108 rushing yards in a 24-17 win over the Ravens.
items.impact: The Saints D/ST tallied three sacks and  one interception in the upset win over the Ravens. The interception was on the Ravens' last offensive play to seal the win for the Saints. New Orleans will take on the Raiders in Week 3.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Daniel Carlson perfect in Week 2 win
items.desc: Daniel Carlson connected on all three of his field goal attempts and his lone extra point attempt in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
items.impact: Carlson connected on field goals from 23, 47, and 51 yards out to help pace the Saints to their first win of the season. The Saints' offense appears to have improved based on their performances over the first two weeks of the season. Carlson should continue to receive plenty of opportunities heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Raiders.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Breece Hall bottled up in Week 2 loss to Packers
items.desc: Breece Hall carried the ball 16 times for 29 yards while also hauling in each of his five targets for 63 yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Hall begins the season as one of the few bright spots in an inconsistent offense, totaling over 90 offensive yards in each of the first two games. The running back remains one of the few reliable options for fantasy managers ahead of a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Juwan Johnson hauls in four passes in Week 2
items.desc: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-4 passes for 66 yards in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
items.impact: Johnson continues to serve as the primary passing option out of the Saints' tight end group. The 30-year-old veteran has topped 50+ receiving yards in the first two games of the season and appears poised to turn in solid performances in an improved Saints' offense. Johnson and the Saints will take on the Raiders in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Geno Smith steady in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Geno Smith completed 27-of-41 pass attempts for 247 yards and one touchdown while also rushing five times for 17 yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Smith took what a strong Green Bay defense allowed Sunday, completing 65.9% of his passes in the loss. The veteran signal-caller will look to take advantage of a generous secondary in a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Devaughn Vele hauls in five passes in Week 2 win
items.desc: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-7 targets for 64 yards in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
items.impact: Vele has put together two solid games to open the season, tallying 12 receptions on 16 targets. Vele is the clear WR2 in the Saints' offense and should be poised for another strong performance against the Raiders in Week 3.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Chris Olave finds the end zone in Week 2 win
items.desc: Chris Olave caught 8-of-10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
items.impact: Olave was considered questionable to play due to a hamstring injury, but that did not appear to impact him at all against the Ravens. Olave caught a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth quarter to tie the game and help pace the Saints to the upset win. Olave will look to continue his strong start to the season in Week 3 against Las Vegas.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Garrett Wilson finds end zone in Week 2 loss to Packers
items.desc: Garrett Wilson hauled in five of his seven targets for 57 yards and one touchdown in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Wilson continues to make the most of sizeable involvement in an underperforming passing attack to begin the season, recording five or more receptions in each of the first two games. The wideout remains one of the more impactful options as part of a Jets offense filled with more questions than answers early on ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Alvin Kamara hauls in five passes in Week 2 win
items.desc: Alvin Kamara rushed for 15 yards on nine carries in the Saints' 24-17 win over the Ravens. He caught 5-of-6 targets for seven yards.
items.impact: Kamara was very limited in his production in his 2026 debut, was clearly a focal point of the offense which cut into Travis Etienne's volume. Fantasy managers will want to be cautious with both running backs volume in question heading into a Week 3 matchup with Las Vegas.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Adonai Mitchell sees 12 targets in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Adonai Mitchell hauled in six of his team-high 12 targets for 63 yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Mitchell has taken advantage of his increased role entering the season in the New York passing attack, recording 60 or more receiving yards in each of the first two games. The wideout looks poised to remain one of quarterback Geno Smith's primary pass-catching options as the season continues, with a Week 3 matchup against the Detroit Lions up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Braelon Allen reaches end zone in Week 2 loss to Packers
items.desc: Braelon Allen rushed five times for seven yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for eight yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Allen made the most of a forgettable performance as part of an underperforming backfield attack Sunday, scoring his first touchdown of the season in a losing effort. The running back remains more of a complementary option behind No. 1 running back Breece Hall for head coach Aaron Glenn, with a favorable Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions up next.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Kenyon Sadiq catches two passes in Week 2
items.desc: Kenyon Sadiq caught two of his three targets for 17 yards in the Jets' 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
items.impact: Sadiq fell back to earth after an impactful Week 1 performance, finishing with less than three receptions in the losing effort. The tight end remains one of many unproven pass-catching options as part of a revamped Jets passing attack ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Tyler Shough executes late comeback win in Week 2
items.desc: Tyler Shough completed 27-of-34 passes for 252 yards and one touchdown in a 24-17 win over the Ravens.
items.impact: Shough also added 23 rushing yards on nine carries in the win. Both of the second-year quarterback's touchdowns came in the fourth quarter to tie the game and give the Saints the lead. Shough has looked great through his first two games of the season and will look to build on these performances in a Week 3 matchup with Las Vegas.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Isaiah Williams sees seven touches in Week 2
items.desc: Isaiah Williams hauled in all six of his targets for 34 yards while also rushing once for 14 yards in the Jets' 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
items.impact: Williams made the most of increased involvement in an underwhelming passing attack, finishing tied for first in receptions in the loss. The wideout remains difficult to trust as another inconsistent pass-catching option ahead of a favorable Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jeremy Ruckert catches two passes in Week 2
items.desc: Jeremy Ruckert caught both of his targets for five yards in the Jets' 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
items.impact: Ruckert has seen minimal involvement in the New York passing attack to begin the season, seeing two targets or less in each of the first two contests. The tight end remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a favorable Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jadarian Price (chest) has X-rays return negative
items.desc: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said X-rays returned negative on Jadarian Price's chest injury.
items.impact: Price left Sunday's game in the second half and did not return, but it is worth noting the game was out of hand. His status will need to be monitored in practice this upcoming week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Sam Darnold (glute) could return to practice this week
items.desc: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold could return to practice this upcoming week.
items.impact: Macdonald clarified it is too soon to know Darnold's status for Week 3 against the Commanders. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week, but it seems unlikely he returns next week as of now.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jayden Daniels suffers dislocated elbow Sunday
items.desc: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said QB Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow.
items.impact: Daniels will undergo additional testing Monday. The X-Rays on Sunday showed no fracture. Marcus Mariota closed out Sunday's game for Washington.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Steelers D/ST allows 14 points in Week 2 loss
items.desc: The Steelers D/ST allowed 14 points, 208 passing yards, and 136 rushing yards in the 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
items.impact: The Steelers' defense did tally an interception, a fumble recovery, and three sacks in the losing effort Sunday. The Steelers' defense will be at home against a strong Bengals' offense in Week 3.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Chris Boswell misses a FG attempt in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Chris Boswell connected on 1-of-2 field goals in the Steelers 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
items.impact: Boswell connected on a 56-yard field goal and missed from 57-yards out in the first quarter. There were reports prior to the game that Boswell was struggling with kicks in pregame warmups, but both his miss and connection were from 55+ yards. Boswell and the Steelers will take on the Bengals at home in Week 3.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Pat Freiermuth hauls in four passes in Week 2
items.desc: Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards and rushed once for two yards in the Steelers 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
items.impact: Freiermuth has logged five targets in both games this season and appears to have built a rapport with Aaron Rodgers. With Michael Pittman dealing with an ankle injury, the veteran tight end could be a solid option heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Bengals.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Germie Bernard leads team in receiving yards in Week 2
items.desc: Steelers WR Germie Bernard caught 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
items.impact: Bernard saw an increase in playing time with Michael Pittman (ankle) unavailable for Week 2. The rookie wide receiver did have a key drop that lead to a Patriots interception. Bernard will look to build on this performance in Week 3 against the Bengals.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Roman Wilson hauls in five passes in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Steelers WR Roman Wilson caught 5-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
items.impact: Wilson has now seen six targets in both games this season and should continue to see an increase in usage as long as Michael Pittman is dealing with an ankle injury. Wilson's five receptions lead the team, but the Steelers' passing attack really failed to get anything consistent going. Wilson and the Steelers will take on the Bengals at home in Week 3.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: DK Metcalf leads team in targets in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Steelers WR DK Metcalf caught 4-of-9 targets for 27 yards in a 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
items.impact: Metcalf was shadowed by Patriots DB Christian Gonzalez for the majority of the game, limiting his production and forcing Aaron Rodgers to look elsewhere. Metcalf has lead the team in targets in the first two games, so the target volume is encouraging, fantasy managers are just waiting for it to result in more production. Metcalf and the Steelers will take on the Bengals in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jordan Love tosses two touchdowns in Week 2 win over Jets
items.desc: Jordan Love completed 16-of-29 pass attempts for 145 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
items.impact: Love continues a solid start to the season as part of a Green Bay offense battling inconsistency early on, throwing two touchdowns in each of the first two games. The quarterback will look for more sizeable success for fantasy managers in a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Christian Watson finds end zone in Week 2 win over Jets
items.desc: Christian Watson hauled in four of his team-high 11 targets for 41 yards and one touchdown in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
items.impact: Watson has been impactful as part of an inconsistent Green Bay offense to begin the season, catching one or more touchdowns on eight or more targets in each of the first two games. The wideout offers fantasy managers one of the few stable options in an underperforming Packer offense ahead of a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.
